requirements.heading: Required Criteria
requirements.text: * Every new top-level type MUST be defined in a Standards Track RFC (see Section 4.9 of RFC 8126 [RFC8126]).

requirements.heading: Required Criteria
requirements.text: * The IANA Considerations section of an RFC defining a new top-level type MUST request that IANA add this new top-level type to the registry of top-level types.

requirements.heading: Required Criteria
requirements.text: * The criteria for what types do and do not fall under the new top- level type MUST be defined clearly.

requirements.heading: Required Criteria
requirements.text: * Any RFC defining a new top-level type MUST clearly document the security considerations applying to all or a significant subset of subtypes.

requirements.heading: Required Criteria
requirements.text: * At a minimum, one subtype MUST be described.

requirements.heading: Negative Criteria
requirements.text: * A top-level type MUST NOT be defined for the mapping of other protocol elements to media types.

requirements.heading: Negative Criteria
requirements.text: A top-level type MUST NOT be defined if its main or only purpose is to map other type systems, e.g., in programming languages or ontologies.

requirements.heading: Negative Criteria
requirements.text: * A new top-level type SHOULD NOT generate aliases for existing widely used types or subtypes.

requirements.heading: Negative Criteria
requirements.text: * Top-level types with an "X-" prefix cannot be registered, and SHOULD NOT be used.

requirements.heading: Security Considerations
requirements.text: The security issues related to introducing a new top-level media type MUST be evaluated and documented carefully.
